api_analysis.hypothesis: The illegal memory access originates from passing host-side std::vector data pointers to CUDA kernels. In the binding, shape.data(), strides.data(), and param_strides.data() are pointers to CPU memory allocated by std::vector. The CUDA kernel dereferences these pointers on the device, causing out-of-bounds access and the reported cudaErrorIllegalAddress.
evidence: diagnostic.json sanitizer shows address 0x1858fe88 is out of bounds, far from any CUDA allocation; this is consistent with a device access to a host pointer.
kernels/custom_ops_binding.cpp constructs host std::vector<int64_t> for shape and strides, then passes .data() directly to the launcher.
custom_ops.cu kernels read shape[d], out_strides[d], x_strides[d], param_strides[d] as device pointers without copying them to device memory.

The input tensors are contiguous with known fixed shapes and strides, so no device-side stride arrays are necessary; precomputing offsets via scalar integer arithmetic on the host eliminates the need for device pointers altogether.
changes: Replace the existing custom_ops.cu with a simplified contiguous implementation supporting only the task's actual dtype and layout: float32, contiguous tensors with fixed shapes as specified in task_contract.json.
Implement abs_forward as a 1D grid-stride kernel over numel using the contiguous linear index.

Implement add_scalar_tensor_forward as a 1D grid-stride kernel where x is contiguous shape [512,3,256,256] and param is contiguous shape [3,256,256]; compute param index as linear index within each batch slice using precomputed constants.
Remove all stride-pointer arguments from launchers; use only raw float pointers, numel, and integer constants (batch, channels, height, width).

Update kernels/custom_ops_binding.cpp to declare the new launcher signatures, remove host stride vectors, pass contiguous tensors after TORCH_CHECK(x.is_contiguous()) and TORCH_CHECK(param.is_contiguous()), and allocate output via torch::empty_like(x).
Keep model_new.py unchanged as it already calls the two custom ops correctly.
